A_target.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a game with finitely many players, each with a [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]] [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] [[Definition:Convex Set (Vector Space)|convex]] strategy set $S_i \subseteq \R^{m_i}$.
Let each payoff $u_i$ be [[Definition:Continuous Mapping|continuous]] and [[Definition:Quasiconcave Function|quasiconcave]] in $s_i$.
Then $\Gamma$ has a [[Definition:Nash Equilibrium|Nash equilibrium]].

B_source.statement:
Let $K \subseteq \R^n$ be [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]], [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] and [[Definition:Convex Set (Vector Space)|convex]].
Let $F: K \to \powerset K$ have [[Definition:Closed Graph|closed graph]] and non-empty convex values.
Then there exists $x \in \map F x$.

substitutions.the compact convex domain: the product of the players' strategy sets
substitutions.a point contained in its own image: a strategy profile in which each player best-responds

derived.the fixed point condition: no player can improve unilaterally, that is, an equilibrium
derived.convexity of the values: quasiconcavity of each payoff in the player's own strategy

object_map.reformulation: Recast mutual best response as membership of a profile in its own image under a set-valued map.

validity_conditions: The product of compact convex sets is compact and convex, so Kakutani applies to the joint strategy space.
The best-response correspondence has nonempty values by continuity of payoffs together with compactness, and convex values precisely because each payoff is quasiconcave in the player's own strategy.
The graph is closed by continuity of the payoffs, which is the remaining hypothesis; quasiconcavity cannot be dropped, since without it best responses may be nonconvex and no fixed point need exist.
proof_plan: Let $S = \displaystyle \prod_i S_i$, which is compact and convex.

Define the [[Definition:Best Response Correspondence|best-response correspondence]]:
:$\displaystyle \map B s = \prod_i \argmax_{t_i \mathop \in S_i} \map {u_i} {t_i, s_{-i} }$
$\map B s$ is non-empty by the [[Extreme Value Theorem]], convex by quasiconcavity, and $B$ has closed graph by [[Berge's Maximum Theorem]].
